output.risk_summary: All three products contain the same type of sedating antihistamine, which significantly increases your risk of dangerous drowsiness, confusion, and falls. Combining them is not safe.

details.finding: Excessive sedating antihistamine exposure from combining multiple products
details.explanation: Benadryl and ZzzQuil both contain diphenhydramine, and Dramamine contains dimenhydrinate, which your body converts into diphenhydramine. Taking all three means you're getting the same drowsiness-causing drug from three different bottles. This dramatically increases your risk of extreme sleepiness, difficulty thinking clearly, dangerous falls (especially for older adults), difficulty urinating, dry mouth, blurred vision, and next-day impairment. In severe cases, this can cause confusion, rapid heartbeat, or difficulty breathing.
details.source: Resolved ingredients analysis and dose accumulation check

details.explanation: We couldn't verify the exact amount of dimenhydrinate in your Dramamine, so your actual total dose of sedating antihistamines may be even higher than calculated. This makes the combination even more unpredictable and potentially dangerous.

output.what_to_do: Choose only one of these products and use it as directed on the label — never combine them. If you need help with allergies, use Benadryl alone (follow package directions, typically 25-50mg every 4-6 hours, not exceeding 300mg in 24 hours). If you need motion sickness relief, use Dramamine alone. If you need sleep help, use ZzzQuil alone. If one product isn't working well enough, do not add another sedating antihistamine. Instead, talk to a pharmacist about a different type of medication that works through a different mechanism. Avoid driving or operating machinery for at least 6-8 hours after taking any of these products.
